title: LTX spatial upscaler - bench evaluation as the SeedVR2 successor
description:
BENCH EVALUATION ONLY - no app work, no plugin, no dropdown. Successor direction to MPI-506, which dropped SeedVR2 on 2026-08-16. Fabio: 'We'll need to explore other ways, like, for example, using LTX Upscaler.'

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT CLASS OF TOOL. MPI-506 measured SeedVR2's two failures as STRUCTURAL, not tuning: (1) it sharpens rather than reconstructs - radial-FFT top/mid 0.57 at 1.5x, 0.43 at 2x, 0.24 at 3x, falling monotonically, against a 1.06 codec control; (2) it has NO semantic prior - one sampling step, cfg 1.0, no text encoder in the weight set - so it deforms eyes (Fabio: 'the iris is almost square'). LTX is a conditioned, multi-step video model, so a regenerative upscale carries the semantic prior SeedVR2 lacks and is prompt-steerable. That is the thesis to test.

EVERYTHING IS ALREADY ON DISK - verified against :8188 /object_info 2026-08-16, not assumed. ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.1.safetensors (0.99 GB) is in G:/CubricModels/latent_upscale_models/; LTXVLatentUpsampler is CORE (comfy_extras.nodes_lt_upsampler); LatentUpscaleModelLoader and LowVRAMLatentUpscaleModelLoader are CORE (comfy_extras.nodes_hunyuan); LTXVTiledSampler / LTXVTiledVAEDecode / LTXVSpatioTemporalTiledVAEDecode ship in ComfyUI-LTXVideo; and the LTX 2.3 checkpoint plus its workflows are already wired. So there is NO download, NO node pack to adopt, NO node_lock.json entry and NO R2 upload - the entire integration tax that made MPI-506 expensive. This card costs bench time only. Signature note: the upsampler takes LATENT + LATENT_UPSCALE_MODEL + VAE and returns LATENT, so it upscales in latent space inside an LTX graph rather than post-processing pixels, and it is x2.

ASK THE VRAM QUESTION FIRST - it is what killed MPI-506, not quality alone. On the 16 GB 4060 Ti, SeedVR2 at 2x on a ~1 Mpx source collapsed frames_per_chunk to 13, and 3x ran only at the temporal floor of 5, taking 1278s for a 2-second clip. Fabio: 'if we're offering a model that can't even do 2x on a 16 GB card, then there's no point in offering it' and '10 minutes for a second, it's just not worth it.' Any LTX result that cannot beat that is not interesting. LowVRAMLatentUpscaleModelLoader and the tiled nodes suggest a better ceiling - hypothesis, not measurement.

THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT is question 2: re-run the radial-FFT top/mid test (with the h264 control) against a fixed lanczos baseline. If LTX also lands well below 1.0 it is the same class of tool as SeedVR2 and the semantic-prior thesis was wrong. Full question list, comparable source clips, and the method traps (laplacian cannot rank two healthy runs; one clip is not enough - MPI-506's fpc=33 'optimum' inverted on the second clip) are in brief.md.

IDEA FOLDED IN 2026-08-16 (same card, test AFTER the main questions): UPSCALE A REDUCED FRAME SET, THEN INTERPOLATE BACK. Fabio's own direction, run manually off 16 fps WAN clips with better results than a straight upscale. It attacks BOTH of the failures MPI-506 measured: fewer frames per pass is the one lever that reliably moves the chunk ceiling (SeedVR2 at 2x collapsed to fpc=13 of 48), and an interpolator ENFORCES the frame-to-frame coherence a short-chunk upscaler cannot - the direct answer to the oscillation on faces. Nothing to install: rife47.pth is on disk and FrameInterpolate + FrameInterpolationModelLoader are CORE (comfy_extras.nodes_frame_interpolation), with RIFE VFI / FILM VFI also available via comfyui-frame-interpolation. Measure FLICKER, not sharpness - and watch for the VFI failure mode, smeared fast motion and thin structures (hair, fingers), so bench a turning face rather than a slow push-in. Note Fabio's WAN case is 'the source was already 16 fps', which is easier than decimating a 24/30 fps clip - do not conflate the two when reading the result. This is a bench idea, not a spec; the app-side shape is a later decision.
